title: Start tasks from the UI, with an optional coding agent and dependency blocking (replaces CS-0005)
summary: Add task dependencies to the record model, a one-click Start action that is blocked until dependencies are done, and an optional sandboxed 'Start with agent' action. Supersedes CS-0005.
rationale: Product owner chose both a Start button and an optional agent launch, and to block Start until a task's earlier work is done. Tasks have no dependency field today, so this adds a depends_on data requirement (REQ-0049 here). It is otherwise the same as CS-0005, plus the blocking criteria (Start AC5, Start with agent AC6). Reject CS-0005 and apply this one.

data.title: Task dependencies
data.statement: The system shall let a task declare the tasks it depends on in a depends_on list of task ids, rejecting unknown ids, self-references and dependency cycles.
data.rationale: Starting a task must be blocked until the work it builds on is done, which needs dependencies recorded on tasks.

acceptance_criteria.text: depends_on accepts ids of existing tasks and rejects an unknown id with a field error
A self-reference or any dependency cycle is rejected with a field error naming the cycle
Deleting a task that another task depends on is refused unless forced, as for other references

data.title: Start task action
data.statement: The system shall offer a Start action on every todo task in the tasks list and the record drawer that moves the task to in-progress in 1 click.
data.rationale: Starting work today means opening the drawer and editing the status field.

acceptance_criteria.text: Start is shown only on tasks with status todo, in the list row and in the record drawer
1 click sets the task to in-progress as a single commit
In the same commit, the task's story and that story's epic move from todo to in-progress; parents that are blocked or done are left unchanged
If the task changed since it was loaded, Start returns 409, the status is unchanged and the row refreshes
While any task in depends_on is not done, Start is disabled and lists the unfinished tasks, and the start route refuses the request with the status unchanged

data.title: Start task with coding agent
data.statement: The system shall, after user confirmation, launch a Claude Code coding agent for a task in its story's component repository on a dedicated branch, briefed with the task, story, requirements and acceptance criteria, and stream its progress to the UI.
data.rationale: Lets a product owner hand a planned task straight to an agent while keeping the work traceable to requirements.

acceptance_criteria.text: A confirmation dialog shows the component path, the branch name reqforge/TASK-NNNN and the full brief; nothing runs until the user confirms
The agent runs via the local claude CLI in a git worktree of the component on branch reqforge/TASK-NNNN
The brief contains the task description and done_when, the story narrative, each linked requirement statement and acceptance criteria, and the trace tag convention
Agent progress streams to the task drawer and the user can cancel the run
When the run ends, the task shows its branch, commits and exit status, and the task status is never set to done automatically
Start with agent is disabled, with the reason shown, when the story has no component, the component has no path, or any task in depends_on is not done

data.title: Coding agent sandbox
data.statement: The system shall confine a task's coding agent to its own worktree and task branch so that 0 commits reach the default branch and 0 files outside that worktree change without human review.
data.rationale: Unlike the chat agent (REQ-0041), the coding agent edits code and runs commands, so its blast radius must be bounded and its runs auditable.

acceptance_criteria.text: An agent run makes 0 commits or pushes to the default branch and pushes only to reqforge/TASK-* branches
An agent run writes 0 files outside its worktree, including the requirements repository
The coding agent has 0 reqforge record-write or changeset-apply tools
Every run is logged with task id, starting user, start and end time, branch and exit status

standards: OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications 2025 LLM06 Excessive Agency

data.done_when: Design reviewed; tool policy denies reqforge write tools and default-branch pushes.

data.description: Create worktree and branch, build the brief, run claude -p with the coding tool policy, stream events, support cancel, write the run log.

data.description: Confirmation dialog with brief preview, disabled state with reason, live progress and cancel in the task drawer, run result summary.

stories: New EPIC-0010 with 3 stories: task dependencies (server, 3 pts), Start button (web, 3 pts), coding agent (server, 8 pts)
code: server: task schema gains depends_on with a cycle check (the schema and validation live in the server model); new start route; the agent launcher can reuse the claude -p invocation in server/src/chat.rs with a separate coding tool policy
web: Start button on task rows and in web/src/components/RecordDrawer.tsx; new agent dialog and run view
New tests: task_depends_on in server/tests/integration.rs, server/tests/agent_run.rs, server/tests/agent_sandbox.rs, web/e2e/suites/task-start.js and agent-start.js (none exist yet)
evals: 4 stories' worth of evals: 5 new evals cover all 18 acceptance criteria of the 4 new requirements
risks: The coding agent edits code and runs commands. The sandbox requirement must be implemented and passing before 'Start with agent' is enabled
Existing tasks have no dependencies recorded. Once depends_on exists, a follow-up changeset should set them (e.g. TASK-0021 and TASK-0022 depend on TASK-0020)
Component records need a path for 'Start with agent' to be usable
CS-0005 must be rejected; applying both would duplicate the requirements
